## Parameters

In BEAST, and under a Tree prior model of Bayesian Extended Coalescent Skyline (BECS), there are a number of parameters estimated at each node in the form of (e.g.) `popSize.alltrees.[number]`. The number of this parameter refers to the node of interest.

In my analyses I am having trouble with these values converging. Looking at these values, I can tell that many of them are very shallow - so I am interested in looking at the taxa attached to these problematic nodes. As an example, I am going to look at the parameter `popSize.alltrees.19` from a phylogeny of Papuan mtDNA. This model is built under the BECS model, with a strict clock, and GTR-4 transition model. As you can see, the parameters estimate seems stable, then starts to jump around alot. It is consistently estimating a depth of around 6,000 years, and then suddenly drops to 700 years.

![](images/Screenshot%202024-06-11%20at%2011.51.20%20am.png){fig-align="center"}

By using the package `treeio` we can import the BEAST output into R, and use that to determine what taxa are linked to the problematic node 19.

The number is

```{r}
library(treeio)

tr = treeio::read.beast("NCI/20240607_mtDNA_CBES/CBES-papua_m.mcct.trees")

library(BioGeoBEARS)
BioGeoBEARS::read

# Function selecting the tip or node name corresponding to the edge row
select.tip.or.node <- function(element, tree) {
    ifelse(element < Ntip(tree)+1,
           tree$tip.label[element],
           tree$node.label[element-Ntip(tree)])
}

BioGeoBEARS::prt(tr@phylo)

## Making the edge table
edge_table <- data.frame(
                "parent" = my_tree$edge[,1],
                "par.name" = sapply(my_tree$edge[,1],
                                    select.tip.or.node,
                                    tree = my_tree),
                "child" = my_tree$edge[,2],
                "chi.name" = sapply(my_tree$edge[,2],
                                    select.tip.or.node,
                                    tree = my_tree)
                )

```

## Different parameterizations to try

This PDF offers an explanation of some other parameters to try:

<http://evomics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/ebsp2-tut.pdf>

#### 1. Changing Populations sizes to 0.5

Since we are analysing mtDNA, only females contribute to the effective population size, which should be approximately half the population.

#### 2. Changing clock rate priors to proper uniform priors

By default, clock rate priors give infinite bounds, but we know that the clock rate will have an upper bound of 1.0. Setting this in the prior will save time and prevent exploration of implausible results.

## BEAST Model Test (bModelTest)

bModelTest is a Bayesian MCMC approach that can switch between time-reversible nucleotide substitution models as well as estimating posterior probability for gamma-distributed rate-heterogeneity and the proportion of invariable sites. This saves us from pre-determining these parameters.

We use the transition and transversion subset of all possible nucleotide reversible models - since it saves us from exploring very unlikely nucleotide changes.

## 20240614 CBES bModelTest

Changes

-   Site model is bModelTest - transitionTransversionSplit - Empirical

-   Strict Clock 2.4065E-8

<!-- -->

-   Population Factor is changed to 0.5 - since mtDNA is only held by half the population

-   populationMean.alltrees has been changed to a 1/x improper prior
